issues.body: The revised comments and proof correctly say that an unsatisfied plain `kani::cover!` is only a report and does not fail verification, but they repeatedly cite `research/mechanized-proof-program.md` §5.1 as the governing discipline. That section still says witness survival is provided by `kani::cover!` and that an unreachable cover "goes red" as a mechanical guard. Thus the implementation and its cited audit requirement disagree on the load-bearing anti-vacuity rule. Because this PR is specifically correcting a soundness misconception in that program, leaving the central record unchanged makes the correction incomplete and can propagate the same vacuity bug to other suites.
issues.fix_hint: Update the cited §5.1 audit/design record in the same PR to distinguish merge-blocking assertions from supplementary cover reports, and revise any requirement text claiming that an unsatisfied plain cover makes the verification verdict fail. Keep the concrete/static assertion requirement as the actual gate.
issues.title: Cited domain-coverage audit record still prescribes the unsound cover-as-gate pattern

verdict.summary: The code-side anti-vacuity fix is materially sound: merge-blocking assertions walk the real static corpus, validate every flagged evader, and pin the named percent-encoded-dot witness; the raised unwind bound also accounts for the concrete string comparison. However, the change is incomplete against the audit record it cites. `research/mechanized-proof-program.md` §5.1 still states that an unreachable `kani::cover!` goes red and mechanically guards pruning, while this diff correctly explains that a plain unsatisfied cover does not fail Kani verification. Leaving the authoritative requirement contradictory invites future harnesses to repeat the exact vacuity defect being fixed. This is a new documentation-consistency finding relative to round 1, so progress is regressing.
